vocabulary_versus_rendered.closed_freshness_vocabulary_authority: RFC2-10, .syzygy/governance/contracts/rfcs/RFC-0002/snapshot-and-evaluation-core.md lines 209-223, quoted from "Four values, closed." to the clause's end: "Four values, closed. The list changes only by amendment to this RFC; no implementation may mint, spell, or force-fit a freshness value it does not carry. The closure is required for the same reason RFC2-24's is: a machine answer carries the freshness state verbatim (RFC6-14), aggregates count per freshness value (RFC6-17), and a disagreement between two renderings over one declared scope is release-blocking (RFC6-22/23) - a value existing in no vocabulary can be neither carried verbatim nor checked for parity, and leaving it unstated is how the value gets chosen by whoever implements the render first. A condition genuinely outside the four is disclosed as a fact of the render, never dressed as a freshness state. Freshness is orthogonal to the three labels and the tier registry; it never substitutes for either." (extended after review 4, finding J1: until then this field stopped at line 214 with no elision marker, while the review-3 disposition said it had been extended)
vocabulary_versus_rendered.freshness_mint_hazard: the freshness twin fires 0 times on this capture because all 713 tuples carry "fresh"; assessCurrency no-bound-declared arm (packages/cap1-core/src/staleness.ts lines 98-104) returns no freshness field, so wiring it - M2 slice 5 - makes line 307 mint a fifth freshness value on every class with no declared bound. RFC2-10 forbids the mint in terms at lines 212-214 ("no implementation may mint, spell, or force-fit a freshness value it does not carry"; an earlier text of this field pointed at line 219, which carries the parity rationale and not the prohibition - corrected after review 5, K3) and, at lines 220-222, supplies the remedy the packet first said it lacked: a condition genuinely outside the four freshness states is disclosed as a fact of the render, never dressed as a freshness state, and lines 222-223 add (the single line 223 named here until review 6, L5) that freshness never substitutes for the labels or the tier registry. So arm (b) of Q2 has three lawful readings for the freshness field, stated here in the packet's own words, which the P-70 row paraphrases clause for clause (an earlier text of this field said "the packet's and register's own words" - corrected after review 5, K6): (b-i) the renderer supplies one of the closed four (M2's Q7, recommending stale with the reason kept distinct); (b-ii) the claim is held Unknown and the tuple is not rendered as though it had a freshness state; or (b-iii) the condition is disclosed as a fact of the render, in a carrier that is not data-epistemic-freshness and is not dressed as a freshness state - the packet's recommendation - and none of them mints a fifth value. An earlier text of this sentence, written in the review-3 repair, enumerated "(b-i) render only the four declared states and no absence, (b-ii) disclose the no-bound-declared condition as a fact of the render beside the tuple, (b-iii) the disclosure route with the absence named in the legend" - three arms that matched neither the packet nor the register; withdrawn after review 4 (finding J3) and kept here marked.
